steps:
The egress IP that Cloudflare sees changed in the last hour. Every factory Cloudflare API token and R2 key accepts calls only from the home IPv4 address. Each one fails until its IP filter allows the new address. CloudflareCredentialRefused names each refused API token. The R2 keys are not tested: a refused R2 key shows through this alert and FactoryHealthStale only.

1. Read the new address. The alert summary names it. From node-1:
curl -s https://api.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace | grep ^ip=

2. In the Cloudflare dashboard, edit the Client IP Address Filtering of each token. Allow the new address and remove the old one. Each name is the token's 1Password item in vault k8s-homelab.
API tokens, checked every minute:
jomcgi-site-cloudflare: the jomcgi.dev deploy token.
factory-health-cloudflare: the health check's read-only Workers token.
factory-cloudflare-api-token: cfgate's Tunnel and DNS token.
R2 keys, not tested:
factory-r2-public-mirror: the public mirror's key. Secrets <mirror>-r2 in factory-public.
r2-s3-public-read: the read-only key in Secret jomcgi-site-r2-read in jomcgi-site-prod and jomcgi-site-dev.
grimoire-migration-r2: the Grimoire migration's read-only key. Secret grimoire-migration-r2 in grimoire.
An edit keeps each token's value, so 1Password needs no change. If you make a new token instead, put it in the 1Password item of the same name (vault k8s-homelab).

3. Wait for the checks. CloudflareCredentialRefused clears at the next accepted check, within 2 min. FactoryHealthStale clears when the mirror copies a new health.json.

No expected address is stored, so there is no value to change: the repository is public and the address is private. The rule compares the addresses of the last hour. It clears 1 h after the change. To clear it sooner, silence FactoryEgressIPChanged in Alertmanager.
